The strongest completed result is now a finite-temperature design criterion for sliding polymer networks: a conserved minimum of mobile spectator rings can remove a specific entropy-driven instability without fixing the sliding junctions. I have kept the nonwinding rotor, its failed cold-looking cases, and the earlier chemistry, kinase and actomyosin results with their corrections and limitations.

I chose this opening after comparing the motor route with reversible polymer networks. The comparison substantially narrows the opportunity: reversible polyrotaxane gels already combine sliding connections with self-healing; asymmetric ring placement already changes mechanical response; and one mobile ring per subchain is already a published model configuration. The candidate contribution is the exact finite-contour criterion and its extension to networks, rather than those broader capabilities. 
ScienceDirect
+2

The completed theoretical result

Starting from the established Gaussian-chain measure with freely sliding rings, I completed the following result:

For a fixed network of three-dimensional Gaussian axles, with conserved total contour on each axle, point junctions, and conserved nonpassing spectator counts, at least one spectator in every constrained interval is sufficient to make the positional free energy convex after integrating over all contour allocations.

The underlying ring-entropy construction is prior work; Chen and colleagues explicitly include free rings and contour fluctuations.

Macromolecules

The sampler passed independent energy and reverse-proposal checks. Earlier traces with an unmodeled end connector were rejected. The corrected boundary and the remaining threading restriction are part of the result’s scope. Monte Carlo moves provide equilibrium sampling, not molecular sliding rates.

Where the chemistry still fails to close

The constructive architecture is an alternating sequence of crosslinkable A rings and spectator B rings, with B guards at both ends. Any fixed subset of A rings could then be linked while retaining at least one spectator in every constrained interval.

Cornelissen’s covalent-template chemistry supplies relevant assembly ingredients: complementary azide/alkyne axle joining, release of temporary ring–axle ester bonds, and selective modification of brominated rings. It does not demonstrate the proposed alternating sliding network. 
pure.uva.nl

Three missing physical operations remain decisive:

Transit: the released rings must slide across the actual terephthalate/linker/triazole joins.
Retention: ring order must survive without the imposed simulation restriction.
Selective connection: coupling A rings must leave B unreactive and preserve the aperture and contour transfer.

The demonstrated A-ring Suzuki reaction is phenylation, not reversible inter-ring coupling. Both released ring types have phenolic hydroxyl groups, so generic hydroxyl-directed linking would undermine the proposed selectivity. 
pure.uva.nl

These are gaps in the construction, rather than consequences of unavailable experimental access. The retained advance is the exact thermal criterion, supported by a bounded explicit-contact test. Its molecular continuation must determine the joint ring–axle statistics—including bending, binding and attachment geometry—from the same physical interactions. A binding constant alone, or another freely chosen effective landscape, would not establish that connection.
